authority_basis.claim_scope: Orthogonal components, sign convention, magnitude and direction reconstruction.

concepts.statement: Component signs follow the declared axis directions and are not inferred from magnitude alone.
concepts.why_required: Signed projections encode direction along each axis.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Components may all be treated as positive and quadrant information is lost.

concepts.statement: A vector must be reconstructable from its components into magnitude and quadrant-correct direction.
concepts.why_required: Reconstruction is the inverse check that component decomposition preserved the original vector.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Incorrect signs or angle quadrants can survive unnoticed.

symbols.name: angle from declared positive x axis

model_conditions.condition: The component relations use orthogonal Cartesian axes.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Cosine and sine projections assume perpendicular basis directions.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: A non-orthogonal basis requires a different projection and reconstruction model.

model_conditions.condition: The angle is measured from the declared positive x direction with a consistent orientation convention.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Component signs and trigonometric projection depend on the angle reference.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: The sine/cosine assignment or signs can be wrong.

representations.semantic_geometry: A vector and its signed orthogonal projections form a component triangle relative to declared x and y axes.
must_not_imply: the acute triangle drawn fixes the actual vector quadrant
representations.verification_method: Reconstruct magnitude and quadrant-correct angle from signed components and compare with the original vector.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Declare axes and sign convention before resolving the vector.
Resolve the vector into signed components in the declared frame.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Later scalar equations can use the wrong component magnitudes or signs.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Reconstruct magnitude and quadrant-correct direction as an inverse check.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: A sign or quadrant error can remain hidden.

required_transformations.description: Translate a vector in declared axes into signed orthogonal components.
Invert the component representation to recover magnitude and quadrant-correct direction.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Components are always positive because magnitudes are positive.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Learners transfer the nonnegative rule for magnitude to signed scalar projections.
trigger_contexts: vectors in quadrant II III or IV
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A vector pointing left has a negative x component while its magnitude remains positive.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Show the vector and signed projections on explicitly labelled positive and negative axes.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Components are signed projections; only the vector magnitude is nonnegative.
misconceptions.verification: Reconstruct with atan2 and check the vector returns to the correct quadrant.

problem_families.name: Resolve a vector into Cartesian components
problem_families.first_technical_move: Declare axes and measure the angle from the stated reference.
fatal_errors: assigning positive components independent of quadrant

problem_families.name: Reconstruct a vector from components
recognition_cues: signed x and y components given
problem_families.first_technical_move: Use the signed components to determine magnitude and quadrant.
